pieces.title: Follow-up: Kitsilano townhouse site walk
pieces.ship: CRM email template or a one-off from Tim

brief.action: Reply to confirm the site walk date and send the scope sheet
brief.proof: Photo report after every visit | $5M liability insurance
brief.length: Under 150 words, one ask, one attachment named
brief.notes: Council president said their current contractor "never sends anything". Property has cedar hedges along the lane and a drainage problem at the north entrance.

tactics.rolls_royce: The president said the current guy "never sends anything". The photo report is the answer to that sentence.

tacticsBrief.name: Find The Fear
tacticsBrief.ask: Name the fear underneath the request. Copy that answers the fear outsells copy that describes the service.
tacticsBrief.standing: Council: a slip claim or a resident complaint with no record to show. Manager: being the one who gets chased. Homeowner: paying for visits nobody can see.

tacticsBrief.name: Simple Sales Story
tacticsBrief.ask: “Someone like you uses this.” Name the kind of customer and what changed for them.

tacticsBrief.name: Rolls Royce Moment
tacticsBrief.ask: One vivid, specific detail that carries the whole claim. Ten general claims lose to it.
tacticsBrief.standing: Pattern: the treasurer who stopped driving over on Thursdays once the photos started arriving. Use a real one from the site walk.
tacticsBrief.answer: The president said the current guy "never sends anything". The photo report is the answer to that sentence.

tacticsBrief.name: Leave It Out
tacticsBrief.ask: Cut anything that doesn’t serve the one action. Especially the second benefit.
